The Elementeita Badlands, also known as the Otutu Forest or Ututu Forest, is a lava flow in Kenya.
The Elementeita Badlands covers approximately 10000 hectares.
The area was previously covered in thick dryland forest characterized by cedar trees, Juniperus spp., and Leleshwa bushes, Tarchonanthus camphoratus.
Wild Jasmine and Boophone are also found in the Elementeita Badlands.
Njenga Karume bought the Elementeita Badlands from Arthur Cole in 1980.
Arthur Cole bought the Elementeita Badlands from Digby Tatham-Warter in 1968.
The Elementeita Badlands is unsuitable for either small scale cultivation or cattle ranching as it is covered in thick bush growing from the profusion of lava boulders.
The Elementeita Badlands can be used as a reference for geographical and ecological studies.

Dzeliwe of Eswatini: Inkhosikati LaShongwe (b. Dzeliwe Shongwe 1927 – 2003) was Queen Regent of Eswatini between 21 September 1982 and 9 August 1983.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: She was a wife of king Sobhuza II of Eswatini, and with him had one child, Prince Khuzulwandle Dlamini.

Dzeliwe of Eswatini: After the death of her husband in August 1982, the Royal Congress named Dzeliwe as Queen Regent, and Prince Sozisa Dlamini as the "Authorized Person", or regent's advisor, until Prince Makhosetive, designated by the king as his successor, reached the age of eighteen.

Dzeliwe of Eswatini: The Liqoqo (a traditional advisory body) supported her regency, but soon there were disagreements between her Prime Minister, Mabandla Dlamini, and other members of Congress led by Mfanasibili Dlamini.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: These problems continued until 25 March 1983, when Prince Mabandla was replaced by Prince Bhekimpi Dlamini.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: Queen Dzeliwe opposed this dismissal, and this led to her being replaced by Ntfombi of Eswatini (the mother of Prince Makhosetive), as regent later that year.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: Prince Makhosetive was crowned on 25 April 1986 with the name of King Mswati III of Eswatini.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: In May, Mswati dissolved the Liqoqo, consolidating his power and reorganising the government.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: In May 1987, twelve people were accused of sedition and treason in relation to the overthrow of Queen Regent Dzeliwe in 1983.
Dzeliwe of Eswatini: King Mswati created a special tribunal to judge these crimes against the King or the Queen Regent, in which the defendants did not have the right to legal representation.

Antonio José de Irisarri: Antonio José de Irisarri Alonso (February 7, 1786 – June 10, 1868), was a Guatemalan statesman, journalist, and politician who served as Interim Supreme Director of Chile in 1814.
Antonio José de Irisarri: He is considered one of the fathers of Chilean journalism together with Fr. Camilo Henríquez.
Antonio José de Irisarri: Irisarri was born in Guatemala City, the son of Juan Bautista de Irisarri and of María de la Paz Alonso.
Antonio José de Irisarri: He studied in his native city and in Europe, from whence he was recalled back to his home after the death of his father in 1805.

Antonio José de Irisarri: In 1809 he visited Chile, and having married Mercedes Trucíos y Larraín, an heiress there, took up his residence in that country and joined with enthusiasm the movement for independence in 1810.

Antonio José de Irisarri: He had charge of important public offices during the struggle for liberty, including the command of the National guard and the civil and military government of the province of Santiago, and from March 7 to 14, 1814, he was temporarily in charge of the supreme direction of the nation.
Antonio José de Irisarri: In 1818 he was appointed Minister of Government and Foreign Affairs by Bernardo O'Higgins, and in October of the same year he went to Buenos Aires as minister.
Antonio José de Irisarri: At the end of 1819 he was sent to Europe to negotiate the recognition of Chilean Independence by England and France (which he was not able to obtain.)
Antonio José de Irisarri: While at London he negotiated a loan of £1,000,000 (the first foreign debt of Chile.)

Antonio José de Irisarri: He was sent to Central America in 1827 as minister for Chile, and in 1837 as plenipotentiary to Peru and private adviser to Admiral Manuel Blanco during the War of the Confederation.
Antonio José de Irisarri: After the Chilean army was forced to sign the Treaty of Paucarpata on November 17, 1837, the scandal was gigantic.
Antonio José de Irisarri: Irisarri refused to return to Chile, was tried "in absentia" for high treason, and sentence to death.
Antonio José de Irisarri: Irisarri wisely never returned to Chile.

Antonio José de Irisarri: He was minister of Guatemala and Salvador to Ecuador from 1839 till 1845, and in 1846-1848 to Colombia, but resigned, and went to Curaçao in 1849, and in 1850 to the United States, where he resided till his death.
Antonio José de Irisarri: The governments of Guatemala and Salvador appointed him, in 1855, their minister to Washington, and for a long time he was dean of the diplomatic corps.
Antonio José de Irisarri: Irisarri continued his literary work in the United States, and was generally esteemed for his knowledge, genial character, and polished manners.

Antonio José de Irisarri: Irisarri was chief editor of the "Semanario Republicano de Chile" in Santiago in 1813; of "El Duende" in the same city in 1818; of "El Censor Americano" in London in 1820; of "El Guatemalteco" in Guatemala in 1828; of "La Verdad desnuda,La Balanza," and "El Correo" in Guayaquil in 1839-1843; of "La Concordia" in Quito in 1844-1845; of" Nosotros,Orden y Libertad," and "El Cristiano Errante" in Bogota in 1846-1847; and of "El Revisor" in Curaçao in 1849, the publication of which he continued in New York.

Antonio José de Irisarri: He also published "La defensa de la historia critica del asesinato cometido en la persona del Gran Mariseal de Ayacucho" (Quito, 1845); "Memoria biografica del Arzobispo Mosquera" (Bogota, 1848); a collection of his satirical poems, a novel, "Cuestiones Filologicas," and several pamphlets.

Antonio José de Irisarri: In 1973 Guatemala honoured him with the institution of an "Order of Antonio José de Irisarri".

Anyone for Doomsday?: is the third full-length album by Powerman 5000, and was originally slated as the follow-up to "Tonight the Stars Revolt!".
Anyone for Doomsday?: It was pulled by PM5K frontman Spider One two weeks before the release date.
Anyone for Doomsday?: Due to being too similar to previous work, the album was originally intended to merely be delayed and revamped.
Anyone for Doomsday?: However, during this time conflicts began to arise causing longtime members Dorian 27 (Dorian Heartsong) and Al3 (Allen Pahanish) to leave the band.
Anyone for Doomsday?: As a result, the album was scrapped due to Spider's unwillingness to release an album of half new members and half old.
Anyone for Doomsday?: The album was available for a while on Powerman 5000's official website through Spider One's record label, Megatronic Records.
Anyone for Doomsday?: The promotional copies featured artwork that was different from the copies available on the website.

Philip II of Spain: Philip II of Spain (21 May 1527 – 13 September 1598) was King of Spain (1556–98), King of Portugal

Philip II of Spain: He was also Duke of Milan, and from 1555, lord of the Seventeen Provinces of the Netherlands.

Philip II of Spain: The son of Holy Roman Emperor and King of the Spanish kingdoms Charles V and Isabella of Portugal, Philip was called "Felipe el PrudentePhilip the Prudent") in the Spanish kingdoms; his empire included territories on every continent then known to Europeans, including his namesake the Philippines.
Philip II of Spain: During his reign, the Spanish kingdoms reached the height of its influence and power.
Philip II of Spain: This is sometimes called the "Spanish Golden Age".
Philip II of Spain: Philip led a highly debt-leveraged regime, seeing state bankruptcies in 1557, 1560, 1569, 1575, and 1596.
Philip II of Spain: This policy was partly the cause of the declaration of independence that created the Dutch Republic in 1581.

Philip II of Spain: On 31 December 1584 Philip signed the Treaty of Joinville, with Henry I, Duke of Guise signing on behalf of the Catholic League; consequently Philip supplied a considerable annual grant to the League over the following decade to maintain the civil war in France, with the hope of destroying the French Calvinists.
Philip II of Spain: A devout Catholic, Philip saw himself as the defender of Catholic Europe against the Ottoman Empire and the Protestant Reformation.
Philip II of Spain: He sent a large armada to invade Protestant England in 1588, with the strategic aim of overthrowing Elizabeth I of England and re-establishing Catholicism there.
Philip II of Spain: He hoped to stop both English interference in the Spanish Netherlands and the harm caused to Spanish interests by English and Dutch privateering.

Philip II of Spain: Philip was described by the Venetian ambassador Paolo Fagolo in 1563 as "slight of stature and round-faced, with pale blue eyes, somewhat prominent lip, and pink skin, but his overall appearance is very attractive".

Serialism of the first type is most specifically defined as the structural principle according to which a recurring series of ordered elements (normally a set -- or row -- of pitches or pitch classes) are used in order or manipulated in particular ways to give a piece unity.

Serialism is often broadly applied to all music written in what Arnold Schoenberg called ``The Method of Composing with Twelve Notes related only to one another ''(Schoenberg 1975, 218; Anon. n.d.), or dodecaphony, and methods that evolved from his methods.
It is sometimes used more specifically to apply only to music where at least one element other than pitch is subjected to being treated as a row or series.
In such usages post-Webernian serialism will be used to denote works that extend serial techniques to other elements of music.
Other terms used to make the distinction are twelve - note serialism for the former, and integral serialism for the latter.

Canadian bitumen does not differ substantially from oils such as Venezuelan extra-heavy and Mexican heavy oil in chemical composition.
Many modern oil refineries can process non-upgraded bitumen directly into products such as gasoline, diesel fuel, and refined asphalt without any preprocessing.

This is particularly common in areas such as the US Gulf coast, where refineries were designed to process Venezuelan and Mexican oil, and in areas such as the US Midwest where refineries were rebuilt to process heavy oil as domestic light oil production declined.

Given the choice, such heavy oil refineries usually prefer to buy bitumen rather than synthetic oil because the cost is lower, and in some cases because they prefer to produce more diesel fuel and less gasoline.

By 2015 Canadian production and exports of non-upgraded bitumen exceeded that of synthetic crude oil at over 1.3 million barrels (210×10^3 m3) per day, of which about 65% was exported to the United States.

The word asphalt is derived from the late Middle English, in turn from French asphalte, based on Late Latin asphalton, asphaltum, which is the Latinisation of the Greek ἄσφαλτος (ásphaltos, ásphalton), a word meaning 'asphalt/bitumen/pitch'.

In French, the term asphalte is used for naturally occurring bitumen-soaked limestone deposits, and for specialised manufactured products with fewer voids or greater bitumen content than the 'asphaltic concrete' used to pave roads.
The first use of asphalt by the ancients was in the nature of a cement for securing or joining together various objects.
Herodotus mentioned that bitumen was brought to Babylon to build its gigantic fortification wall.
The word passed from Greek to late Latin, and thence into French (asphalte) and English ('asphaltum' and 'asphalt').

Deuteronilus Mensae is a region on Mars 937 km across and centered at.
Deuteronilus Mensae covers 344°–325° West and 40°–48° North.
Deuteronilus region lies just to the north of Arabia Terra and is included in the Ismenius Lacus quadrangle.
Deuteronilus Mensae is along the dichotomy boundary, that is between the old, heavily cratered southern highlands and the low plains of the northern hemisphere.
Deuteronilus Mensae contains flat-topped knobby terrain that may have been formed by glaciers at some time in the past.
Deuteronilus Mensae is to the immediate west of Protonilus Mensae and Ismeniae Fossae.
Glaciers persist in the Deuteronilus Mensae region in modern times, with at least one glacier estimated to have formed as recently as 100,000 to 10,000 years ago.
Recent evidence from the radar on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter has shown that parts of Deuteronilus Mensae do indeed contain ice.

Shiraz: The second half of the 19th century witnessed certain economic developments that greatly changed the economy of Shiraz.
Shiraz: The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 allowed the extensive import into southern Iran of inexpensive European factory-made goods, either directly from Europe or via India.
Shiraz: Farmers in unprecedented numbers began planting cash crops such as opium poppy, tobacco, and cotton.
Shiraz: Many of these export crops passed through Shiraz on their way to the Persian Gulf.

records.text: Adam R. Dell was born on 1970-01-14.
Adam R. Dell is an American venture capitalist.
Adam R. Dell is the brother of Michael Dell.
Michael Dell is the founder of computer manufacturing company Dell Inc.
Dell Inspiron is a laptop and desktop computer brand.
Dell's reputation for poor customer service was established since 2002.
Dell's growth outstripped its technical support infrastructure, leading to increased scrutiny on the Web.

Dell's original model was known for high customer satisfaction when PCs sold for thousands but by the 2000s, the company could not justify that level of service when computers in the same lineup sold for hundreds.
Rollins shifted Dick Hunter from head of manufacturing to head of customer service in response to Dell's poor customer service.
Dick Hunter aimed to reduce call transfer times and have call center representatives resolve inquiries in one call to improve customer service.
Dell spent $100 million in just a few months to improve customer service and rolled out DellConnect to answer customer inquiries more quickly.
In July 2006, Dell started its Direct2Dell blog to improve customer service.
In February 2007, Michael Dell launched IdeaStorm.com, asking customers for advice to improve customer service.
These initiatives managed to reduce negative blog posts from 49% to 22% and reduce the prominence of 'Dell Hell' on Internet search engines.
Dell was founded in 1984 by Michael Dell while he was a student at the University of Texas at Austin.
Dell's initial business was selling IBM PC-compatible computers built from stock components.
Dell dropped out of the University of Texas at Austin to focus on his business after receiving $1,000 from his family.
In 1985, Dell produced the first computer of its own design, the Turbo PC, which sold for $795.
Dell's initial business model involved advertising in national computer magazines and custom assembling each ordered unit.
Dell's first year of operation grossed more than $73 million.
Chittoor Mohammed Habeebullah was born in 1937 in the South Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India.
Upon independence in 1947, the title of Viceroy was abolished and the representative of the British Sovereign became known as the Governor-General.
C. Rajagopalachari was the only Indian Governor-General after independence.
After India's independence, the Governor-General's role became largely ceremonial, with the Indian cabinet exercising power on a day-to-day basis.
In 1950, India became a republic and the President of India took over the functions previously performed by the Governor-General.
Ashok Kumar Mago is the founder and Chairman of the US-INDIA Chamber of Commerce, formerly known as the Greater Dallas Indo American Chamber.
Milkha Singh was born on 1935-10-08.
Milkha Singh was known as The Flying Sikh.
Milkha Singh was an Indian former track and field sprinter.
Milkha Singh was introduced to the sport while serving in the Indian Army.
Milkha Singh was the only Indian athlete to win an individual athletics gold medal at a Commonwealth Games until 2010.
Milkha Singh won gold medals in the 1958 and 1962 Asian Games.
Milkha Singh represented India in the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome and the 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo.
Milkha Singh was awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honour, in recognition of his sporting achievements.
K. Shivaram Karanth was born on 10 October 1902.
K. Shivaram Karanth died on 9 December 1997.
K. Shivaram Karanth was a novelist in the Kannada language.
K. Shivaram Karanth was a playwright.
K. Shivaram Karanth was a conservationist.
Ramachandra Guha referred to K. Shivaram Karanth as the 'Rabindranath Tagore of Modern India' and called him one of the finest novelists-activists since independence.
K. Shivaram Karanth was awarded the Jnanpith Award for Kannada, the highest literary honor in India, for his work.
K. Shivaram Karanth's son is Ullas, who is a conservationist.
The Jnanpith Award is the highest literary honor conferred in India.

Arthur Chung was honoured with Guyana's highest national honour, the Order of Excellence (O.E.).
During his time as President of Guyana, the office was that of a ceremonial head of state, with real power in the hands of Prime Minister Forbes Burnham.

Lata Mangeshkar was born on 28 September 1929.
Lata Mangeshkar is an Indian playback singer and occasional music composer.
Lata Mangeshkar's career started in 1942 and has spanned over seven decades.
Lata Mangeshkar has recorded songs for over a thousand Hindi films and has sung songs in over thirty-six regional Indian languages and foreign languages, primarily in Marathi and Hindi.
Lata Mangeshkar has received three National Film Awards, 12 Bengal Film Journalists' Association Awards, four Filmfare Best Female Playback Awards, and many more.
Lata Mangeshkar received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1989 from the Government of India.
Lata Mangeshkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian honour, by the Government of India.
Lata Mangeshkar has four siblings: Asha Bhosle, Hridaynath Mangeshkar, Usha Mangeshkar, and Meena Mangeshkar, with Lata Mangeshkar being the eldest.

Lokesh Kumar Singhal was honored by the Government of India in 2012 with the Padma Shri.
